source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, making it the second-largest declared data center in Virginia and 7.2% of the state's total published capacity.

Virginia has 1,603 MW of declared IT capacity across 25 facilities that state specifications, but 330 data center facilities are mapped in the state. Sterling's 116 MW is concentrated in one campus, and the fact that only 25 of 330 sites publish power figures means the published total undercounts the state's actual capacity. For AI, a 116 MW power budget could support roughly 2,900 accelerator racks at 40 kW per rack, but the operator's specifications do not state actual tenant equipment or utilization, so this is a ceiling rather than a measure of deployed compute.

The published specifications omit total power draw, PUE, cooling technology, grid interconnection details, and any expansion constraints. No certifications are listed. Whether this campus is currently constrained by power supply or grid availability in Northern Virginia is not stated, so the data cannot confirm or rule out grid limits on this site.
